items.text: If a data center is camouflaged in the woods, will anyone hate it?
items.article: By planting gardens and restoring ecosystems around its data centers, Microsoft thinks it can be a “better neighbor.” But is it enough? Microsoft is expanding ‘biomimicry’ at its data centers as it faces more pushback from locals over construction, pollution, and noise. San Antonio City Councilmember Ric Galvan remembers when data centers first arrived in his city in the 2000s, looking like relatively unassuming office buildings. But that’s changed in recent years, as data centers have grown into massive “hyperscale” facilities spanning millions of square feet and housing the physical infrastructure for AI. There are now more than a dozen data centers in Galvan’s roughly 55-square-mile district, and he expects that number to grow to around 20 over the next few years if proposed projects are completed. They’re clustered along two main roads, concentrating nuisances in the same neighborhoods: traffic and trees cut down during construction, followed by constant bright lights and noise when the data center is operating. A lot of the area used to be green fields, he explains, allowing many residents to feel close to nature. items.text: After bankruptcy, he was banned from sports betting sites. Then he discovered Kalshi
items.article: The dark side of the prediction market boom is becoming more clear: Experts say the sites have become go-to outlets for gambling addicts to relapse as the companies avoid state consumer protections. During the pandemic, Thomas thought he would give DraftKings and FanDuel a try. Before long, he formed a habit. "I could have ten drinks one night and then be fine with not drinking again for a year," said Thomas, 35, who asked to be identified by his middle name fearing his problem gambling history could affect his career. "But sports gambling was different. It really got me." He never cared much for sports. Yet betting on games seemed like an easy way to make a buck. He started placing wagers on football and tennis mostly using parlays, which are difficult-to-win bets that require multiple things happening in one game in order to land an enticing payout. Working from his home in Pennsylvania in the financial services industry, Thomas says there were few moments when he didn't have one eye on placing a bet as he juggled work emails and meetings. When his paycheck arrived, he'd quickly squander it all trying to dig himself out of a gambling hole, only to find himself even deeper in. This cycle continued for years, with Thomas racking up around $75,000 in debt from credit cards and personal loans. He ended up more than $50,000 in the red from online sportsbooks.

items.key: ai:christa pike survived attempted execution. what now?
items.text: Christa Pike survived attempted execution. What now?
items.article: The nation is awaiting answers after the botched execution of murderer Christa Pike on Sept. 30 resulted in her hospitalization in critical condition. Pike, 50, survived two rounds of lethal injection drugs and was taken by ambulance to a hospital, her attorneys have said. “We don’t have much sense of her prognosis but we do know that she is alive right now and receiving lifesaving medical care,” Randy Spivey, one of Pike’s attorneys, said on Oct. 1. Attorneys said her condition was unchanged as of late the night of Oct. 1. USA TODAY has reached out to Pike's legal team on Oct. 2 for any updates to her status. Tennessee officials have meanwhile said little about Pike's health condition or how the lethal injection could have failed. The Department of Correction said it followed protocol. The failed execution prompted Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to call for an independent investigation and put a pause on executions in the state for the remainder of the year. He called what happened in Pike's death chamber "disturbing" and a "tragedy." "How does that happen?" he said on Oct. 1. "It shouldn’t be very difficult." Pike was to be put to death for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend brutally tortured and killed Slemmer. The execution attempt came after a chaotic day of last-minute legal wrangling that went all the way up to the U.S. Supreme Court.

items.text: What is happening with diesel – and should we be worried?
items.article: Donald Trump has threatened to ban US diesel exports of diesel – here’s what that could mean Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Diesel prices in the UK have reached a record high, according to the RAC, hitting £2 a litre for the first time as the war in the Middle East continues to drive up the cost of oil worldwide. The price of a litre in the UK has risen 40.5 per cent since late February, when the US first launched strikes against Iran, while prices are also at a record high in the US, where much of the world’s supply is produced and refined. In response to rising costs, Donald Trump has indicated he will ask European countries to draw from their diesel reserves as he threatens a ban on US exports of the fuel. Since 2022, the US has become the world’s largest exporter of diesel by a wide margin as the Ukraine conflict has reduced demand for Russian fuel, alongside its ability to refine it. Around 30 per cent of all cars on the road in the UK are fuelled by diesel, rising to 38 per cent of HGVs. Higher costs to operate these vehicles could have an impact on the cost of goods.

items.article: Anthony Gordon has been England's in-form player since the World Cup knockout stage - is the Barcelona forward now undroppable? All have become guaranteed starters and reliable stars for England, with the Barcelona winger the latest to look, according to captain Kane, like one of the Three Lions' "main men". Gordon was one of England's standout players at the World Cup and earned a big-money move to European giants Barca in the summer, while his good form has continued into his country's Nations League campaign. He scored the opening goal in England's 2-0 win against the Czech Republic on Tuesday night, after also netting in a 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday. In fact, the 25-year-old's England form has been building since the knockout stage of the World Cup began - his run of averaging a goal contribution every 69 minutes started with assisting both Kane's efforts in a 2-1 last-32 victory over DR Congo. CJP has raised question about electoral rolls and how the Election Commission function. Dipke has defended the decision to hold the agitation on 2 October, referring to Mahatma Gandhi's role in India's freedom movement. Allison Feldman returned to her Arizona home after running errands on a typical Tuesday on Feb. 17, 2015. But when the 31-year-old's family and boyfriend did not hear from her later that evening into the following day, they knew something was wrong. "We talked almost every day," her father, Harley Feldman, told local ABC affiliate reporters. "My wife said, it's just not right, things were out of normal." Concerned for his daughter, Harley called Scottsdale Police for a welfare check on her. At the same time, unbeknownst to Harley, Feldman's boyfriend, Alex Stone, went to her house in Scottsdale and found her dead on the floor, naked and bloodied. items.key: ai:as texas declares state of emergency over fuel shortage, what's dyed diesel?
items.text: As Texas declares state of emergency over fuel shortage, what's dyed diesel?
items.article: As global oil supplies continue to tighten up amid ongoing geopolitical conflicts that have pushed up fuel prices, the governor of Texas has declared a state of emergency. If you get Global News from Instagram or Facebook - that will be changing. Find out how you can still connect with us . As global oil supplies continue to tighten and fuel prices soar , the governor of Texas declared a state of emergency over a shortage of diesel fuel. Declaring a state of emergency can unlock a government’s ability to temporarily modify certain policies in order to protect the general public: in the case of Texas, this includes waiving restrictions on what’s known as dyed diesel. Governor Greg Abbott of Texas issued an emergency notice on Monday. “The shortage of diesel fuel poses an imminent threat or occurrence of harm to the public health and safety in the State of Texas,” the notice says. “A shortage of diesel fuel will impose harmful effects upon the agriculture and ranching industries by increasing the price per acre to achieve similar yields, reducing investment in farm and ranch machinery, and driving up supply chain expenses.”

items.text: I quit ADHD meds after they made me WORSE… why so many are ditching pills
items.article: FOR the millions of Brits with ADHD, a daily stimulant tablet holds the potential to unlock a new world - one that is quieter, less chaotic, with a... FOR the millions of Brits with ADHD, a daily stimulant tablet holds the potential to unlock a new world – one that is quieter, less chaotic, with a level playing field. The surge in prescription drugs for ADHD has been explosive in the past few years. But for some, it’s not all it’s cracked up to be. Others are spooked by little-known risks on the heart and even death, leaving them searching more desperately for answers to manage symptoms. When Michelle Akpata, 30, was diagnosed with ADHD, she hoped a prescription from her GP would rid her of the extra load she’d been carrying for years. “It often felt like running a marathon mentally just to stay organised throughout the day,” says Michelle, a broadcaster and radio presenter from London . “I realised that my difficulty maintaining focus and structure wasn’t just stress, but a consistent pattern affecting my day-to-day life.” But after starting Ritalin (10mg), the initial surge in energy gave way to troubling side effects.
